summary: Starter Story 'How I Work' profile of Jay, a former Amazon software engineer who built a meetup app for solo travellers, expats and nomads. He says it launched about 15 months earlier, makes about $140k a month, has 1.8 million users and over 100k meetups, and was bootstrapped as a solo founder. Most of the video covers his daily routine, working from cafes while travelling, and staying close to users (e.g. four months in Bangkok). Key takeaway: build something you care about, stay on the ground with your users, and treat regret as the bigger risk.

tactics.name: Dogfood on the ground in your core market
steps: Travel to the app's biggest hotspot (he spent four months in Bangkok)
Attend meetups through your own app
Talk to users to find feature ideas and underserved sub-segments

quote.text: going to meet up to my own app and talking to people. And I got so many ideas for new things to add
quote.speaker: Jay

tactics.name: Work in focused blocks with breaks and location changes
steps: Check phone first for anything broken or time-sensitive
Two hours locked in on the top task
Take breaks to re-centre; move location after 3-4 hours

quote.text: after three, four hours, even one place like I need to just move
quote.speaker: Jay

warnings.warning: Products that mature often drift away from the original problem they solved; stay grounded with users.

quote.text: as they mature, they kind of like lose track of the ball and distance themselves from the original kind of good product
quote.speaker: Jay

warnings.warning: Working only for money or status on something you do not enjoy will be miserable.

quote.text: if you're putting all your life's effort and select something that you don't enjoy, like just to make money
quote.speaker: Jay

lessons.lesson: Having a safety net (a big tech job you could get again) lowers the real risk of trying; regret can be the bigger risk.

quote.text: It felt more risky to me to not try. Cause then I would be like full of regret
quote.speaker: Jay

lessons.lesson: Being physically among your users generates better feature ideas and reveals sub-segments.

quote.text: I got so many future ideas by just being in Bangkok
quote.speaker: Jay

lessons.lesson: Passion is a competitive advantage: someone having fun every day is hard to out-compete.

quote.text: if you're just having fun every day with work, it's very, very hard to compete with you
quote.speaker: Jay

lessons.lesson: Hours have diminishing returns without breaks; breaks restore full focus.

quote.text: my hours have diminishing returns if I don't take bricks
quote.speaker: Jay

lessons.lesson: You can build things very fast now and test ideas alongside a job.

quote.text: you can build stuff for so fast and just go out there and try. You can even do stuff at the same time as your work

lessons.lesson: A non-entrepreneur engineer can bootstrap a consumer app to large scale as a solo founder.
